% A guard: it checks cases that the fix of files read with the primitive
% \input from a package of the document must not break.
% Files of the document that give a .4ht's name in \ProvidesFile, read
% from packages of the document. As in the PDF, each file's text is in
% the page, and tex4ht reads no .4ht of those names. index.4ht defines
% \printindex and framed.4ht defines \MakeFramed, which the PDF does not
% have, so the page shows that one was read: a sentence the PDF does not
% have.
% - test-ownprim-guards.sty, beside the document, reads
%   test-ownprim/glossary.tex, named like glossary.4ht, with LaTeX's
%   braced \input.
% - test-ownprim/sty/test-ownprimsub.sty, loaded by its path, reads
%   test-ownprim/index.tex, named like index.4ht, with the primitive
%   \input.
% - test-ownprim/path/test-ownprimpath.sty, found through \input@path,
%   reads test-ownprim/framed.tex, named like framed.4ht, with the
%   primitive \input.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{test-ownprim-guards}
\usepackage{test-ownprim/sty/test-ownprimsub}
\makeatletter
\def\input@path{{test-ownprim/path/}}
\makeatother
\usepackage{test-ownprimpath}
\begin{document}
Braced: \ownprimglossary\par
Subfolder: \ownprimindex\par
Path: \ownprimframed
\ifdefined\printindex\par Index read for the web.\fi
\ifdefined\MakeFramed\par Framed read for the web.\fi
\end{document}
